Harkesh Manuja J. (Oral)

1.  This order will dispose off present six appeals bearing RFA Nos. 820 to 825 of 2000 (O&M) filed at the instance of appellants- landowners, as all arise out of common award dated 21.01.1999 passed by the Reference Court-cum-Additional District Judge, Faridabad.

For convenience, the facts are being taken from RFA-820- 2000 (O&M).
2.

By way of present appeal(s), challenge has been laid to an award dated 21.01.1999, passed by the Reference Court, whereby, petition(s) filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for brevity, "1894 Act") at the instance of appellants-landowners, seeking enhancement of compensation qua acquisition of their land, stand dismissed.
3.

Briefly stating, land measuring 3.76 acres and 19.69 acres came to be acquired vide notifications dated 07.11.1979 and 29.08.1979 respectively, issued under Section 4 of the 1894 Act, followed by notifications dated 17.12.1979 and 18.09.1979, respectively, issued under Section 6 of the 1894 Act,
falling within the revenue estate of village Rahimpur, Tehsil Palwal, District Faridabad.
The land was acquired for the public purpose i.e. for the High level bridge over Yamuna river near village Rahimpur.

The Land Acquisition Collector vide award dated 27.03.1980 awarded the compensation as under:-

"Compensation at the rate of Rs.9280/- per acre of Chahi land, Rs.4000/- per acre for Bud land in respect of land measuring 3.76 acres, thereby, awarding compensation of Rs.26832.85 paise which included price of the land and 15%
solatium and as regards 19.96 acres of land, LAC awarded same rate in respect of Chahi and Bud Land and Rs.7200/- per acre for Magda land."

4. Aggrieved thereof, the appellants-landowners filed reference petition(s) under Section 18 of the 1894 Act and vide judgment dated 21.01.1999, the Reference Court-cum-Additional District Judge,
Faridabad, dismissed the same.
5. Feeling dissatisfied, the appellants-landowners filed the present appeal(s).

6. Impugning the aforementioned award dated 21.01.1999, the sole submission raised by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of appellants- landowners is that the Reference Court fell into error while discarding award dated 03.06.1998 (Ex.P-5) passed in relation to acquisition of land carried out vide notification dated 22.05.1978 for the land pertaining to village Kithwari, Tehsil Palwal,
District Faridabad, whereby the market value for the land acquired therein was assessed at the rate of Rs.33,000/- per acre.

He further submits that the revenue estate of villages Kithwari and Rahimpur, District Palwal, then District Faridabad, are in close proximity and thus, the award dated 03.06.1998 (Ex.P-5) should have been considered by the Reference Court while determining compensation regarding the present acquisition.
No other argument has been addressed.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel representing the respondent- State vehemently opposes the claim set-up in the present appeal(s) while submitting that the evidence available on record was appreciated in proper 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:087126 RFA-820-2000(O&M) --4-- perspective by the Reference Court while passing the impugned award, which thus warrants no interference.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the paper book.
I am unable to find substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellants-landowners.
9. Acquisition in the present case relates to village Rahimpur whereas the award dated 03.06.1998 (Ex.P-5) relates to acquisition of land falling within the revenue estate of village Kithwari.

Neither any aks shajra nor any site plan has been produced or proved on record by the appellants- landowners, so as to compare the location of the two parcels of land; one forming part of present acquisition and the other forming part of award dated 03.06.1998 (Ex.P-5).
No other reliable evidence has been produced on record by the land-owners to establish on record that the potential and locational value of both the parcels of land was comparable.

10. In such circumstances, the Reference Court committed no illegality or perversity while not relying upon the award dated 03.06.1998 (Ex.P-5) for the purpose of assessment of compensation regarding the acquisition in the present case.
